heuristics.rule: Master's degree graduates (any program length) receive a 3-year PGWP effective February 15, 2024
heuristics.condition: When an international student completes a master's degree at an eligible Canadian DLI on or after February 15, 2024
heuristics.action: Apply for a 3-year PGWP regardless of whether the master's program was 1 year or 2 years in length
heuristics.because: IRCC changed the PGWP duration rule for master's degrees effective February 15, 2024 — previously a 1-year master's yielded only a 1-year PGWP
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC PGWP program page; IRCC press release February 15, 2024

heuristics.rule: PhD graduates receive a 3-year PGWP regardless of program length effective February 15, 2024
heuristics.condition: When an international student completes a doctoral (PhD) degree at an eligible Canadian DLI on or after February 15, 2024
heuristics.because: IRCC updated the PGWP duration rule for doctoral degrees effective February 15, 2024
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC PGWP program page; IRCC press release February 15, 2024

heuristics.rule: Programs of 8 months to under 2 years yield a PGWP equal to the length of the program
heuristics.condition: When an international student completes a program of 8 months to under 2 years (other than a master's or PhD)
heuristics.action: Expect a PGWP matching the program's duration, not a fixed 3-year term
heuristics.because: IRCC duration rules post-February 15, 2024 only grant automatic 3-year PGWPs to master's, PhD, and programs of 2 years or longer
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC PGWP program page; IRCC press release February 15, 2024

heuristics.rule: Programs of 2 years or longer yield a 3-year PGWP
heuristics.condition: When an international student completes a program of 2 years or longer (other than master's or PhD)
heuristics.because: The 3-year PGWP for programs 2 years or longer was unchanged by the February 15, 2024 updates
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC PGWP program page; IRCC press release February 15, 2024

heuristics.rule: Bachelor's degree graduates must have studied in an eligible field of study to receive a PGWP effective November 1, 2024
heuristics.condition: When an international student graduates from a bachelor's degree program starting on or after November 1, 2024
heuristics.action: Verify that the field of study is on the IRCC-approved eligible fields list before applying for PGWP
heuristics.because: IRCC implemented field of study requirements for bachelor's level graduates effective November 1, 2024; 178 fields were removed from eligibility
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC field of study requirements for PGWP; IRCC notice November 1, 2024

heuristics.rule: Master's and PhD graduates are exempt from the field of study requirement
heuristics.condition: When an international student holds a master's or PhD degree from an eligible Canadian DLI
heuristics.action: Apply for the 3-year PGWP without regard to field of study
heuristics.because: IRCC explicitly exempts master's and PhD graduates from the field of study requirement introduced November 1, 2024
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC field of study requirements for PGWP

heuristics.rule: PGWP applicants who apply before their study permit expires may work under maintained status while the application is pending
heuristics.condition: When a PGWP application is pending and the graduate applied before their study permit expired
heuristics.action: The graduate may work under the maintained status provision during the approximately 8-month processing period
heuristics.because: IRCC's maintained status provision preserves work authorization during a pending PGWP application provided the application was filed before study permit expiry

heuristics.rule: LMIA-backed job offer points have been removed from the Express Entry CRS effective Spring 2025
heuristics.condition: When an Express Entry candidate holds an LMIA-backed job offer after Spring 2025
heuristics.action: Do not count on receiving 50 or 200 additional CRS points for that job offer
heuristics.because: Minister Marc Miller announced December 18, 2024 that arranged employment points via LMIA route were removed from the CRS to address fraud and increase fairness
heuristics.regulatory_basis: Minister Marc Miller announcement December 18, 2024; IRCC Express Entry updates

heuristics.rule: Work in NOC TEER 4 or 5 does not count toward CEC eligibility even if full-time and legally authorized
heuristics.condition: When a PGWP holder is employed in a NOC TEER 4 or TEER 5 occupation (e.g., retail sales clerk, food service worker)
heuristics.action: Recognize that this employment does not accumulate CEC-eligible Canadian work experience regardless of hours or duration
heuristics.because: CEC eligibility requires work in NOC TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3; TEER 4 and TEER 5 are explicitly excluded from CEC qualifying experience
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC CEC requirements; NOC TEER system

heuristics.rule: Students in bachelor's programs affected by the November 1, 2024 field of study removal may have transitional protection if they started before that date
heuristics.condition: When a bachelor's degree student began a program in a field removed from PGWP eligibility before November 1, 2024
heuristics.action: Assess eligibility for transitional protection before assuming PGWP ineligibility
heuristics.because: IRCC indicated that students in affected programs who started before November 1, 2024 may have transitional protection
heuristics.regulatory_basis: IRCC field of study requirements for PGWP

decision_factors.factor: Degree level (master's/PhD vs. bachelor's vs. other)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines both PGWP duration and whether field of study eligibility rules apply
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Master's and PhD graduates receive automatic 3-year PGWP and are exempt from field of study requirements. Bachelor's graduates must meet field of study criteria. Other program graduates receive PGWP equal to program length (if 8 months to under 2 years) or 3 years (if 2 years or longer).

decision_factors.factor: Field of study (bachelor's level graduates only)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether a bachelor's graduate is eligible for a PGWP at all under post-November 1, 2024 rules
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the program appears on the IRCC-approved eligible fields list. 178 fields including many general business, liberal arts, and some social science programs were removed effective November 1, 2024.

decision_factors.factor: Program start date relative to November 1, 2024
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether transitional protection applies for bachelor's students in fields removed from PGWP eligibility
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Students who started before November 1, 2024 in an affected program may have transitional protection; students who started on or after that date in a removed field are not eligible

decision_factors.factor: NOC TEER level of Canadian employment
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether work experience counts toward CEC eligibility in Express Entry
decision_factors.how_to_assess: TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3 = CEC-eligible. TEER 4 or 5 = not CEC-eligible, even if full-time and legally authorized under PGWP.

decision_factors.factor: Timing of PGWP application relative to study permit expiry
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether the graduate can work legally during the approximately 8-month PGWP processing period
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Application must be submitted before the study permit expires to access maintained status work authorization during processing

decision_factors.factor: French language proficiency (TEF Canada or TCF Canada)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: French language bonus remains in effect in CRS and is now one of the most impactful CRS optimizations available following removal of LMIA job offer points
decision_factors.how_to_assess: TEF Canada or TCF Canada scores can add 25-50+ CRS points

decision_factors.why_it_matters: A provincial nomination adds 600 CRS points, guaranteeing an Invitation to Apply (ITA), and is more important now that LMIA job offer points are removed
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess alignment with specific PNP stream requirements for the candidate's occupation, work location, and province

decision_factors.factor: Core CRS factors: language (CLB/IELTS), education, age, Canadian work experience
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Following the removal of LMIA job offer points, these core factors are the primary determinants of CRS score
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Candidates compete purely on these factors without the ability to supplement via arranged employment LMIA route

hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: The approximately 8-month PGWP processing time runs regardless of when the application is submitted; graduates who wait months before applying effectively lose that period from their authorized PGWP term before it is even issued
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: All PGWP-eligible graduates, particularly those in shorter programs who receive a PGWP equal to program length rather than a fixed 3 years

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting TEER 4 or TEER 5 employment under a PGWP
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Time spent in TEER 4 or 5 work (e.g., retail, food service) is legal and generates income but does not accumulate CEC-eligible Canadian work experience, meaning the PGWP clock runs without building the 1 year of skilled experience required for Canadian Experience Class
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: PGWP holders who work in retail trade, food services, or accommodation — the top sectors where PGWP holders are employed according to IRCC data

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Relying on an LMIA-backed job offer to boost CRS score post-Spring 2025
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: IRCC removed all arranged employment CRS points via the LMIA route effective Spring 2025; a valid LMIA-backed offer no longer yields 50 or 200 additional CRS points
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Express Entry candidates who planned to use an LMIA job offer as a CRS shortcut, particularly those with lower core CRS scores

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Completing a 1-year master's program in Canada
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Under pre-February 15, 2024 rules, a 1-year master's yielded only a 1-year PGWP. Under the updated rules, it yields a 3-year PGWP — graduates who completed their program before the February 15, 2024 effective date may not benefit from this change
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: International students who completed 1-year master's programs before February 15, 2024

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Enrolling in a bachelor's program in a general business, liberal arts, or certain social science field
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: 178 fields including many general business, liberal arts, and some social science programs were removed from PGWP eligibility effective November 1, 2024; bachelor's graduates in these fields are no longer eligible for a PGWP
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Bachelor's degree students who started programs in removed fields on or after November 1, 2024

failure_patterns.pattern: Bachelor's graduate applies for PGWP after completing a program in a field removed from eligibility on or after November 1, 2024
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: IRCC removed 178 fields from PGWP eligibility effective November 1, 2024; bachelor's graduates in these fields no longer qualify for a PGWP
warning_signs: Program is in general business, liberal arts, or certain social science fields
Program started on or after November 1, 2024

failure_patterns.pattern: Graduate submits PGWP application after study permit has already expired
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Maintained status work authorization during PGWP processing is only available if the application was filed before study permit expiry
failure_patterns.consequence: Loss of authorization to work legally during the approximately 8-month PGWP processing period; potential loss of immigration status
warning_signs: Graduate delays PGWP application by weeks or months after convocation
Study permit expiry date is approaching or has passed at time of application

failure_patterns.pattern: PGWP holder works only in TEER 4 or TEER 5 occupations for the full duration of their PGWP
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: TEER 4 and TEER 5 work is legally permitted under a PGWP but is explicitly excluded from CEC-eligible work experience
failure_patterns.consequence: PGWP holder fails to accumulate the 1 year of skilled (TEER 0-3) Canadian work experience required for Canadian Experience Class eligibility; PGWP expires without achieving permanent residency pathway through CEC
warning_signs: Employment in retail trade, food services, or accommodation throughout PGWP period
No effort to secure TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3 employment

failure_patterns.pattern: Express Entry candidate pays for or relies on LMIA-backed job offer to boost CRS score after Spring 2025
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Some immigration consultants sold fraudulent or inflated LMIA letters; IRCC removed LMIA arranged employment points from the CRS effective Spring 2025 to address this fraud vector
failure_patterns.consequence: No CRS points awarded for LMIA-backed job offer; financial loss if fees were paid for LMIA; potential fraud exposure if LMIA was purchased
warning_signs: Candidate was advised by consultant to obtain LMIA-backed offer for CRS boost after December 18, 2024 announcement
Candidate is counting on 50 or 200 CRS point uplift from job offer

diagnostic_questions.question: Did the applicant complete a master's or PhD degree at an eligible Canadian DLI on or after February 15, 2024?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Eligibility for automatic 3-year PGWP and exemption from field of study requirements
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant is eligible for a 3-year PGWP with no field of study restriction; proceed to assess PGWP application timing
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Determine degree type and program length to assess applicable PGWP duration rule; if bachelor's level, assess field of study eligibility

diagnostic_questions.question: If the applicant is a bachelor's graduate, did they start their program before or after November 1, 2024?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether transitional protection may apply for students in fields removed from PGWP eligibility
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If started before November 1, 2024 in an affected field, assess transitional protection eligibility
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If started on or after November 1, 2024, verify that the field of study is on the current IRCC-approved eligible fields list

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the applicant's bachelor's field of study on the IRCC-approved eligible fields list post-November 1, 2024?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: PGWP eligibility for bachelor's degree graduates under the updated field of study requirements
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant is eligible for a PGWP; assess program length to determine duration
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant is not eligible for a PGWP unless transitional protection applies (started before November 1, 2024)

diagnostic_questions.question: Did the applicant submit their PGWP application before their study permit expired?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the applicant can legally work in Canada under maintained status during the approximately 8-month PGWP processing period
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant may work under maintained status while PGWP is pending
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant may lack authorization to work during processing and may have a status issue; urgent remediation required

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the PGWP holder's current employment classified as NOC TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the work experience is accumulating toward the 1 year of skilled Canadian work experience required for CEC eligibility
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Employment is CEC-eligible; track hours and duration toward the 1-year CEC threshold
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Employment in TEER 4 or 5 does not count toward CEC; candidate must secure TEER 0-3 employment to build Express Entry profile

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the Express Entry candidate relying on an LMIA-backed job offer for additional CRS points after Spring 2025?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether the candidate's CRS strategy accounts for the removal of LMIA arranged employment points
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Candidate must revise CRS strategy; LMIA job offer no longer yields CRS points; focus on core factors, French language, or PNP pathway
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Candidate is building CRS score through available mechanisms; assess French language score and PNP eligibility as highest-impact remaining options

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the Express Entry candidate have TEF Canada or TCF Canada scores documenting French language proficiency?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Eligibility for French language CRS bonus, which can add 25-50+ points and is now one of the most impactful CRS optimizations available
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Calculate French language CRS bonus and incorporate into overall CRS assessment
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Candidate should assess feasibility of obtaining French proficiency to access this CRS advantage given removal of LMIA points

industry_realities.common_belief: A 1-year master's program in Canada yields only a 1-year PGWP
industry_realities.actual_reality: Effective February 15, 2024, any master's degree — regardless of program length — yields a 3-year PGWP. A 1-year master's now produces the same 3-year PGWP as a 2-year program.
industry_realities.implication: International students who completed or are completing 1-year master's programs on or after February 15, 2024 have significantly more time to accumulate the 1 year of skilled Canadian work experience needed for CEC

industry_realities.common_belief: Any degree from a Canadian DLI qualifies a bachelor's graduate for a PGWP
industry_realities.actual_reality: Effective November 1, 2024, bachelor's degree graduates must have studied in an IRCC-approved eligible field. 178 fields including many general business, liberal arts, and certain social science programs were removed from eligibility.
industry_realities.implication: Bachelor's graduates in removed fields who started after November 1, 2024 are not eligible for a PGWP; program selection now directly determines post-graduation work authorization

industry_realities.common_belief: Working legally in Canada on a PGWP accumulates Canadian work experience toward CEC regardless of job type
industry_realities.actual_reality: Only work in NOC TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3 counts toward CEC eligibility. Work in TEER 4 or 5 (e.g., retail sales, food service) is legal under a PGWP but does not accumulate CEC-eligible experience.
industry_realities.implication: PGWP holders must secure skilled employment (TEER 0-3) — not just any legal employment — to build a qualifying Express Entry/CEC profile before their PGWP expires

industry_realities.common_belief: Securing an LMIA-backed job offer is a reliable strategy to boost CRS scores in Express Entry
industry_realities.actual_reality: Effective Spring 2025, IRCC removed all LMIA-based arranged employment points from the CRS. The previous 50-point and 200-point bonuses are no longer available.
industry_realities.implication: Candidates who planned to use an LMIA job offer as a CRS shortcut must rebuild their Express Entry strategy around core CRS factors, French language proficiency, and PNP pathways

industry_realities.common_belief: The PGWP is issued quickly after graduation, so there is no urgency in applying immediately
industry_realities.actual_reality: IRCC reports PGWP processing times of approximately 8 months as of mid-2025. Graduates who delay applying lose usable PGWP time before the permit is even issued.
industry_realities.implication: Graduates should apply for their PGWP the same week as graduation to avoid burning authorized work time during the processing period

industry_realities.common_belief: Most PGWP holders work in jobs aligned with their field of study
industry_realities.actual_reality: IRCC data shows a significant portion of PGWP holders work in sectors not aligned with their field of study, with top employment sectors being Retail Trade, Food Services and Accommodation, and Healthcare.
industry_realities.implication: Having a PGWP does not guarantee field-relevant employment; graduates must proactively pursue TEER 0-3 roles aligned with their field to build CEC-eligible experience

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Understanding PGWP duration for master's graduates
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Assumes a 1-year master's program yields a 1-year PGWP and advises students to do a 2-year program for a 3-year PGWP
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Knows that effective February 15, 2024, any master's degree yields a 3-year PGWP regardless of program length; does not recommend extending program duration solely for PGWP purposes
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Incorrect advice may lead students to enroll in longer, more expensive programs unnecessarily when the same PGWP outcome is achievable with a 1-year master's post-February 15, 2024

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Field of study requirement awareness for bachelor's graduates
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Advises any bachelor's graduate from a Canadian DLI that they qualify for a PGWP
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Checks whether the specific field of study is on the IRCC-approved eligible list and confirms the program start date relative to November 1, 2024 before advising on PGWP eligibility
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Advising a student in a removed field that they qualify for a PGWP leads to incorrect post-graduation planning and potential status issues

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: CEC-eligible work experience vs. any legal work under PGWP
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Tells PGWP holders that any full-time legal employment in Canada counts toward Express Entry/CEC requirements
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Distinguishes explicitly between TEER 0-3 (CEC-eligible) and TEER 4-5 (not CEC-eligible) employment; advises PGWP holders to prioritize TEER 0-3 roles to build qualifying experience within their PGWP window
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: A PGWP holder who spends their entire work authorization in TEER 4-5 employment accumulates zero CEC-eligible experience and may exhaust their PGWP without a viable permanent residency pathway through CEC

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Advises Express Entry candidates to obtain an LMIA-backed job offer to boost their CRS score by 50-200 points
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Knows LMIA arranged employment points were removed from the CRS effective Spring 2025; redirects candidates to optimize core CRS factors, French language proficiency (TEF Canada/TCF Canada for 25-50+ points), and PNP streams as the remaining high-impact strategies
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Advising candidates to pursue LMIA job offers for CRS points post-Spring 2025 results in wasted effort and potential exposure to consultant fraud; correct advice requires knowledge of the December 18, 2024 policy change

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Tells graduates they can apply for their PGWP at any point after graduation and the 8-month wait is just administrative
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Advises graduates to apply for their PGWP the same week as graduation because the 8-month processing period runs from application date, not from permit issuance; also confirms application must be submitted before study permit expiry to access maintained status work authorization
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Late application burns usable PGWP time and, if submitted after study permit expiry, eliminates maintained status work authorization during the processing period
